(1) the Two Alternate Questions Random Response model is the most efficient model when π Y (the population proportion with the nonsensitive attribute Y) is not known, and (2) when π Y is assumed to be known, the one sample single Alternate Questions model is the most effective.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of eliciting information from respondents in surveys about their sensitive attributes, i.e. attributes that are socially or legally undesirable, such as drug use or criminal activity.
a new two-sample model for estimating the proportion of the population with a sensitive attribute, and with a comparison of this model with other two and one sample models.
the development of an alternative to Moors' model for the case when the population proportion with the nonsensitive attribute is not known in a priori and two randomization samples are available.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Two Alternate Question model is the most efficient when π Y is unknown, but when π Y is estimated from the same survey, the One Alternate Question model is more efficient.

the Two Alternate Questions Random Response model is superior to the Single Alternate Question model when π Y, is unknown, and that the Two Sample Single Alternate Question Random Response model is the superior model when π Y, is known.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
when π A is the parameter of interest, the two alternate questions randomized response model is superior to the one sample model with a known π Y.
the present model is superior to Moors' version of the two-sample single alternate question model.

The main takeaway from our work is that

when π Y is unknown the two sample single alternate model is more efficient than the one sample single and two sample single alternate models, but the two sample single and two alternate model is more than 10% more efficient than the two sample single alternative model, and more than 30% more efficient than either one of the one sample models.

the optimum estimator for the two sample model has the same efficiency as Moors' estimator, and that the two sample model is more efficient than the one sample model when the population proportion with the nonsensitive attribute is unknown.

when the population proportion with the sensitive attribute is small, and when the nonsensitive alternate questions are chosen well, the Two Alternate Questions Random Response model is more efficient than the standard model and is also more efficient than the One Sample Single Alternate Question model when the population proportion π Y is known.
